title: Master Headless Tools
objectives: Navigate the Headless Tools directory and filter by category
Evaluate a listing for agent-readiness (docs, auth, machine-readable specs)
Integrate one directory tool into an AI agent via function calling

modules.title: Find and Shortlist Tools
steps: Open headless.tools and filter the directory by one category you'll actually use (e.g., email, payments, or web scraping)
Open 3 listings and record each tool's base API URL, auth method, and free tier limits in a notes file
Discard any listing whose docs require a human UI flow (OAuth consent screens you can't automate, dashboard-only config)

modules.title: Assess Agent-Readiness
steps: For each shortlisted tool, check its docs for an OpenAPI spec, MCP server, or structured JSON error responses — note which exist
Read the rate limits and webhook docs; write down how an agent would retry a 429 and verify a webhook signature
Pick a winner by scoring the 3 tools 1-5 on spec availability, error format, and idempotency-key support

modules.title: Test the API Headlessly
steps: Sign up for your chosen tool, mint an API key, and store it in a .env file (never hardcode it)
Run the docs' 'hello world' endpoint with curl, piping the response through jq to confirm the JSON shape matches the docs
Deliberately send one malformed request and one request without the key; confirm both return machine-readable error codes

modules.title: Wire It Into an Agent
steps: Write a JSON-schema function definition (name, description, parameters) that wraps the endpoint you tested
Register the function with your agent framework (OpenAI tools, Anthropic tool use, or LangChain) and run a prompt that triggers it
Add a guardrail: cap calls per run, and log the agent's raw tool-call arguments for one test session to catch hallucinated parameters

Have built at least a basic AI agent or chatbot with tool/function calling

modules.title: Setup & First Video Analysis
steps: Install the google-genai Python SDK, set your GEMINI_API_KEY env var, and initialize a client with gemini-2.5-flash
Upload a short (<2 min) MP4 using client.files.upload(), then poll client.files.get() until state is ACTIVE before generating
Send the file reference plus a prompt like 'Summarize this video and list every distinct scene' to client.models.generate_content() and print the result

modules.title: Timestamped & Structured Output
steps: Prompt for timestamps explicitly: 'For each event, return start and end in MM:SS format' and verify Gemini grounds answers to video timecodes

Ask a question about a specific window ('What happens between 0:45 and 1:10?') and compare answers at default vs. low media resolution to see token/accuracy tradeoffs (~300 tokens/sec default, ~100 at low)

modules.title: Building the Agentic Video Loop
steps: Declare 2-3 tools with function declarations, e.g. log_event(timestamp, label) and request_rewatch(start, end), and pass them via the tools config
Run a generate_content call where the model watches a video and decide which tools to call; parse the returned function_call parts from the response
Execute the requested functions in your code, send results back as function_response parts, and continue the conversation until the model returns a final text answer

modules.title: Long Videos, YouTube & Production Hardening
steps: Analyze a YouTube URL directly by passing file_data with file_uri set to the video link instead of uploading
For long-form files, split analysis by prompting per-chunk summaries first, then a second pass that reasons over the combined structured notes
Add retries around file polling and generation calls, log per-request token usage from response.usage_metadata, and set a cost ceiling per video

prerequisites: Intermediate Python (environments, SDKs, JSON handling)
A Google AI Studio API key
